A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 22-17: PUBLIC FACILITIES IMPACT FEE PROGRAM
  UPDATE – PREPARED BY ROBERT SPENCER, dba URBAN ECONOMICS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the draft Public Facilities Impact Fee
  Program (attached) and direct staff to bring back the appropriate ordinance to revise
  Chapter 17.74 of the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code and the appropriate
  resolution(s) to adopt the new fees as set forth in the Program.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and provided
  an overview of the proposed modifications to the impact fee program including the option
  of adding an Art Impact Fee and Multi-modal Traffic Impact Fee.

  Discussion ensued concerning the Park Fee and how an Art Impact Fee would be
  implemented. Robert Spencer commented that it would be in lieu of requiring art in a
  space accessible to the public as a component of any non-residential zone development
  and is typically a percentage of the building permit fee used to enhance the aesthetic
  value.

  Further discussion ensued concerning implementing a Multi-modal Traffic Impact Fee
  instead of a Traffic Impact Fee. Mr. Spencer commented that some cities, typically those
  that are built out and do not have room to expand capacity for vehicles, are moving
  toward a Multi-Modal Traffic Impact fee where the focus is on non-vehicle modes of
  transportation. He explained that this type of fee can be used for the entire
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 26, 2018
   transportation system including things like sidewalks and bike lanes, in addition to
  intersection and capacity improvements.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ regarding the library fee, Mr. Spencer
  explained that the fee is a pass through fee.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the option to implement a Multi-modal Traffic
  Impact Fee. In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding the current Traffic
  Impact Fee in the commercial district, Planning Director Wahba explained that traffic
  impacts will be analyzed to determine how to use those fees. Mr. Spencer further
  explained how the various traffic impact fees could be used to address CEQA impacts.

  NO ACTION WAS TAKEN. CITY COUNCIL DIRECTED STAFF TO EXPLORE THE
  OTHER IDEAS DISCUSSED INCLUDING AN ART IMPACT FEE AND MULTI-
  MODAL TRAFFIC IMPACT FEE AS COMPARED TO THE CURRENT TRAFFIC
  IMPACT FEE AND BRING THE MATTER BACK FOR FURTHER DISCUSSION IN
  A WORKSHOP FORMAT.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 29-16: CONSTRUCTION HOURS FOR PV PENINSULA
  WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH BETWEEN
  DAPPLEGRAY LANE AND MONTECILLO DRIVE

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) open the public hearing; (2) take public
  testimony; (3) discuss the issues; (4) close the public hearing; and (5) approve California
  Water Service Company’s request to shift work between Dapplegray Lane to Montecillo
  Drive from overnight work to daytime work, subject to final approval by the City’s Traffic
  Engineering Deputy.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the nighttime intersection work at Palos Verdes
  Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East. In response to MAYOR HUFF, Cal Water
  representatives indicated that the nighttime work in that area would last approximately
  one week.

  Discussion ensued concerning the noise analysis. COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN
  pointed out that the noise analysis does not incorporate the impact of using sound walls
  to reduce the noise. Further discussion ensued concerning the traffic impacts of
  switching the work to daytime work specifically during the school year. In response to
  MAYOR HUFF, Assistant City Manager commented that Cal Water is in discussion with
  PV Transit regarding the use of bus service to Dapplegray Elementary School to reduce
  the number of vehicles.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 26, 2018
   MAYOR HUFF called for public comment.

  Robert Kuta, VP Engineering for Cal Water addressed the City Council to thank the
  COUNCIL and staff for their continued support.

  Carmelo Sorce, Director of Engineering, California Water Service Company explained
  the noise impact study and reasons for the request to shift the work for a portion of the
  project from nighttime work to daytime work. He commented that although not shown
  in the presentation, the use of noise barrier walls was included in the noise analysis but
  did not significantly impact the noise levels based on the feasibility of installing such
  barriers. He further reviewed the benefits of switching the work to daytime work which
  include preventing more than 800 families from being affected by nighttime construction
  noise, saving millions of dollars in potential relocation costs and increased safety due to
  increased visibility during daytime hours.

  Mr. Sorce further reviewed the various other options considered including adding crews
  and increasing work hours to shorten the duration of the project, noting that
  unfortunately due to availability of pipe, that is not an option. He further reviewed traffic
  animation showing the traffic impact of the switch to daytime work.

  Discussion ensued concerning the traffic impacts at Dapplegray Elementary School and
  Miraleste Intermediate School. In response to COUNCILMEMER SCHMIITZ, Assistant
  City Manager Grammer commented that currently the bus service is proposed for
  Dapplegray Elementary only. Mr. Sorce commented that Cal Water can look at bus
  options for Miraleste Intermediate School.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the traffic impacts of daytime work and how the
  traffic signal timing and use of traffic officers could be used to minimize the traffic
  impacts.

  Traffic Engineer Itagaki reviewed the traffic plans for the proposed daytime work
  including the options for signal timing adjustments to increase east and westbound
  traffic flow and the use of traffic control officers with the lights on flashing red to
  physically monitor traffic flow and make adjustments as necessary.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that the options before the COUNCIL seem
  limited.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed concern that the noise study did not
  incorporate the use of sound barriers and that the traffic impacts of daytime work will
  affect a larger number of people. Discussion ensued concerning the reliability of the
  noise analysis and the use of sound barriers.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JUNE 26, 2018
   MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL suggested that the noise analysis be reviewed by a third
  party.

  In response to the COUNCIL’S concern regarding the noise analysis, Justin Skarb with
  California Water Service Company clarified that the noise study did incorporate the use
  of sound walls which had a minimal impact on the noise levels.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that it would be helpful to have the person
  that conducted the sound analysis present to answer these questions. In response to
  the suggestion for a third party review of the data, Senior Planner Naughton commented
  that that staff could ask ESA, the company that did the initial study MND, if they could
  conduct a peer review of the noise analysis.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the options before the COUNCIL including the
  possibility of adjusting the work scheduled to daytime work based on the noise impacts
  realized and the logistics involved with the use of sound walls. Discussion ensued
  concerning continuing the public hearing to a date specific to allow for a third party
  review of the data and potential dates for such continuance.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  RE-OPEN AND CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO JUNE 5, 2018 AT 4:00
  P.M. WITH A REQUEST TO STAFF AND CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE
  COMPANY FOR FURTHER INFORMATION REGARDING THE NOISE ANALYSIS
  RELATED TO THE NIGHTTIME WORK

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

B.  FY 2018-19 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) open the public hearing and take public
  testimony related to the budget adoption including: appropriation limit, fees and
  charges, fund balance policy and investment policy; (2) close the public hearing; and (3)
  review and adopt Resolution 2422 – adopting the consolidated budget; Resolution 2423
  – establishing the 2018-19 fiscal year appropriation limit; Resolution 2424 –
  establishing schedule of municipal fees and charges; and statement of Fund Balance
  Policy and Statement of Investment Policy

  City Manager Prichard and Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a brief
  staff report (as per agenda material.) Discussion ensued concerning the options for
  which data to use in adopting the appropriations limit with the COUNCIL concurring to
  use the change in California per capita personal income as the inflation factor and the
  growth of the County as the population factor as presented in Resolution 2423.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
JUNE 26, 2018

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE RESOLUTION 2422 ADOPTING THE
  CONSOLIDATED BUDGET.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE RESOLUTION 2422 ADOPTING THE
  CONSOLIDATED BUDGET.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE RESOLUTION 2423 ESTABLISHING THE
  2018-19 FISCAL YEAR APPROPRIATION LIMIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
